description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became rather than as a batch job: no EXEC PGM= names it anywhere under app/jcl or app/proc, and all four of its call sites are online - CORPT00C :392 and :412, COTRN02C :393 and :413. LS-DATE='XX220719  ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='<XX>YYMMDD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (:84-:85), each written out to the full PIC X(10) width because the declared width changes the outcome; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (:86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no SELECT and opens no file, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, leaves no final state and takes no job parameter - its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes :97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity :98 moves into RETURN-CODE, which is 3 here and is not normalised to 4, 8 or 12. This is arm 4 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at :128, matched at :135 and moving 'Invalid Era    ' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) at :136, with WHEN OTHER still last at :147; the arm order is itself the contract, because EVALUATE takes the first matching WHEN. Severity 3 and message 2509 are DECODED from that arm's own 88-level VALUE X'000309CD59C3C5C5' at :65 - the two leading halfwords 0x0003 and 0x09CD = 9*256+205, followed by the severity-control byte and the facility identifier 'CEE' - and are never interpolated from a neighbouring arm, because the nine message numbers are non-contiguous: 2507, 2508, 2509, then a jump to 2513, so counting on would give 2510, which no arm names. The result literal is reproduced verbatim from :136 including the four trailing spaces the COBOL author wrote inside the quotes, and the run of five spaces before 'TstDate:' is those four plus the one-byte FILLER at [35,36). WS-DATE at [45,55) carries the :122 defect deliberately: MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE is a GROUP move whose source opens with Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY, so the ten-byte receiver takes two binary bytes - written explicitly as \u0000\u000A below, the declared length 10 that :105 moved in as a halfword - and then only the first eight characters of the date, overwriting what :107 had placed there. WS-DATE-FMT at [66,76) stays clean, because :111-:113 set it before the CALL and :122 targets WS-DATE alone. An era field is declared by the angle brackets and occupies two input bytes; 'XX' is not one of the two supported era names, which is precisely the condition this arm reports. The mask is exactly ten characters ON PURPOSE: LS-DATE-FORMAT is PIC X(10), so '<XX>YYYYMMDD' would be truncated to '<XX>YYYYMM' and would then report 2507 for want of a day rather than the 2509 it appears to ask for - a real trap, and the reason a two-digit year is used here. Do not read this as the general far-past case: an unrecognised era name is 2509, whereas a date the era admits but the supported Lillian range does not is 2513 - case10 ('1582-10-14' with 'YYYY-MM-DD', the day before the epoch) and case11 ('BC220719  ' with '<BC>YYMMDD'). The three share severity 3 and so the same RETURN-CODE, but they carry different message numbers and different result texts and cannot be collapsed: 2513 is the one error both callers accept (CORPT00C :399, COTRN02C :400), so folding 2509 into it would turn a rejected date into an accepted one. All thirteen WS-MESSAGE spans declared at :42-:57 were summed mechanically to exactly 80, and INITIALIZE at :90 does not clear a FILLER, so the three literal VALUE clauses appear in every output. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the lines cited here and are not captured from, recorded against or replayed from any COBOL execution: this environment provides no Language Environment CEE* service, so CEEDAYS cannot be called at all.
